claims.sentence: <jats:p><jats:bold>Objective </jats:bold> To determine whether prophylactic, low dose controlled‐release aspirin improves outcome for pregnant women and their babies in Barbados.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:bold>Design </jats:bold> Randomised placebo‐controlled trial.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:bold>Setting </jats:bold> The Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Barbados.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:bold>Population </jats:bold> All women attending antenatal clinics between 12 and 32 weeks of gestation were eligible, if without specific contraindications to aspirin and unlikely to deliver immediately.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:bold>Methods </jats:bold> Randomisation was computer‐generated in the antenatal clinic; 1822 women were allocated to receive 75 mg controlled‐release aspirin and 1825 matching placebo.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:bold>Main outcome measures </jats:bold> Proteinuric pre‐eclampsia, other pregnancy‐induced hypertension, pregnancy duration, birthweight, stillbirths and neonatal deaths, major neonatal events.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:bold>Results </jats:bold> All but three women from each group were followed up successfully.
